metadata.name: chgrp
metadata.description: Change the group ownership of files

installation.note: chgrp is commonly available by default as part of GNU coreutils

overview.summary: The chgrp command changes the group ownership of one or more files or directories. You must be the file owner or root to change the group; the new group must be one you belong to (unless root).
when_to_use: Give a file or directory to a different group (e.g., www-data, developers)
Fix group ownership after copying files
Set group for shared project files

syntax.description: GROUP can be a group name or numeric GID. Use -R to change recursively.

options.description: Change group recursively for directories and their contents
options.use_case: Apply group ownership to an entire directory tree

options.description: Report only when a change is made
options.use_case: See which files were actually changed

options.description: Output a message for every file processed

examples.title: Change group of a file
examples.description: Set the group of script.sh to 'developers'
examples.use_case: Share a file with a group

examples.title: Change group recursively
examples.description: Set group www-data on the web root and all contents
examples.use_case: Web server needs group access to all site files

common_pitfalls.description: Only the file owner or root can change group; you can only set a group you belong to (unless root).
common_pitfalls.solution: Use sudo when changing system files or when setting a group you are not in.

related_commands.description: Change both owner and group (e.g., chown user:group file)
